# Paper package: one honest, reproducible results package for the learner / graph / selection line

Branch `claude/paper-package-20261013` (cut from `claude/redteam-20261013`; result trees and documents of `claude/graph-mechanism-20261013` and `claude/graph-endpoint-1013` were copied in unchanged). **Nothing was re-run**: every table and figure is generated from the stored result files by the scripts in `graph_exploration/PAPER_PACKAGE/` (`make all`); every number in the prose is checked against the generated tables by `check_prose.py`. `code/ACADEMIC_REPORT_DRAFT.md` is untouched. This document is assembled by `build_docs.py`; edit `prose/*.src.md`, never this file.

## 0. How to read this
- **Status words** (never stronger than the frozen rule / the data): *PRE-REGISTERED, CONFIRMED* = the success rule written before the confirmation seeds existed was met in the primary block (further blocks: replicated / partly / not replicated); *PRE-REGISTERED, NOT CONFIRMED*; *DESCRIPTIVE* = computed on confirmation seeds but not itself a frozen test; *DEVELOPMENT OBSERVATION* = development seeds only (selected on the same seeds); *AUDIT* = red-team development audit; *DOCUMENTED ONLY* = earlier protocol, numbers not regenerated here.
- **Gains** are paired over seeds on identical label sets (mean over budgets 10/20/40/60 and 3 label draws); intervals are 95% bootstrap over seeds; splits A / B are the two held-out designs. Same 168 labelled groups re-split in every seed: intervals and p-values are optimistic (section 4).
- **Pre-registration order** was verified from git history: for 24 of 25 (study, result directory) pairs the frozen pre-registration file was committed before the first commit of the confirmation result directory (`tables/prereg_order.md`); the remaining 1 is a red-team confirmation directory (`rt/c_a2`) that did not exist in the git history when the package was built. Commit time is not file-creation time: the check shows ordering of commits, not that no cell existed earlier (the studies state they did not).

### What to put in a paper, in three tiers
- **Safe headline claims** (pre-registered, replicated, and not an anchor-copy artefact): anchor weighting (L1, L2; for aw8_all the anchor-far AUC gain is +0.020 / +0.034 in the red-team confirmation block; aw8 alone has an anchor-far check only in the development block); selection rules are absorbed by a tuned learner (S1 vs S2/S3).
- **Claims to hedge**: the Laplacian learner and the long schedule (L3 to L5) are confirmed on the standard endpoint, but the red-team audit shows the gain is uneven across anchor-distance strata (strong anchor-near, about zero in the middle bands, positive again beyond 0.03; threshold-dependent) and that the longer schedule's extra gain is anchor-near (R1; a time-blocked split keeps the gain: R3); the graph's own share beyond generic regularisation is small and unconfirmed (D2); HTR gains are fragile (L13, S4 to S6).
- **Do not claim**: that more unlabelled images keep helping (G4), that beating a shuffled graph proves the graph structure matters (L8, G3), a graph advantage on the paper's own type-accuracy endpoint (G6), robustness to unseen growth runs or samples (only three runs exist; harsh-split tests use fixed small test sets, G5).

## 2. Draft abstract-level summary (English; also `PAPER_PACKAGE/ABSTRACT_EN.md`)
# Draft abstract-level summary (English)

*Every number carries a marker that names its key in `tables/numbers_*.json`; `check_prose.py` fails if a number does not match. Status words follow the claims table (`tables/claims_table.md`).*

**Setting.** We study how well a reward model trained on a few pairwise (pair, type) judgments predicts held-out judgments of RHEED reconstruction types, with frozen SimCLR features and 10 to 60 added judgments. All experiments use one small data set: 168 labelled pair groups (521 judgments) over 284 frames of 3 growth runs; every "new seed" is a new random re-split of these same groups, so p-values are optimistic and only pre-registered confirmations on unused seeds count as evidence.

**What was confirmed (pre-registered, 35 unused seeds per block, splits A / B).** (i) Raising the weight of the reference-anchor loss from 0.25 to 8 improves held-out AUC by +0.012 / +0.019 over the default head; using all ideal images as anchors gives +0.020 / +0.023. (ii) A Laplacian regulariser on a cosine-kNN graph of unlabelled frames adds +0.015 / +0.014 AUC on top of the anchor-weighted learner (replicated in an independent block and from a cold start), and training the head for four times as many steps adds a further +0.010 / +0.007. (iii) The resulting learner beats a graph-free learner whose schedule was tuned by +0.021 / +0.016 AUC and +0.023 / +0.020 accuracy (primary test; replicated). (iv) Acquisition rules matter only for a weak learner: pool-wide variance-reduction selection beats random selection with the default head (AUC +0.010 / +0.013), but with the best learner no pre-registered rule does (vopt_u: +0.001 / −0.001 AUC).

**What the graph does and does not explain.** The gain of the graph regulariser falls as the graph is corrupted (per-seed Spearman between gain and graph quality +0.76 / +0.67, confirmed in two blocks); a shuffled graph is far worse than no graph (AUC −0.128 / −0.126 against the baseline), so beating a shuffled control is a low bar. In development a graph-free consistency regulariser at the same long schedule comes within −0.005 / −0.007 AUC of the best learner, so the graph's own share is small and unconfirmed. Adding unlabelled frames helps only up to about 10% of the trajectory frames (the formal trend test passes, the plateau check says more frames do not help).

**Limits that change how the results should be read.** Held-out frames are near-duplicates of training frames, and 47% of held-out judgments involve an image within cosine distance 0.001 of a typed ideal image. On the red team's confirmation block (35 unused seeds) the gain of the best learner over the tuned graph-free control is +0.035 / +0.037 AUC for these anchor-near judgments, about zero in the bands 0.001 to 0.03 from the nearest anchor (−0.002 / −0.002 at 0.01 to 0.03), and +0.019 / +0.013 AUC (accuracy +0.029 / +0.029) where both images are farther than 0.03 from every anchor; with the red team's own stricter far threshold of 0.01 the AUC gain is only +0.003 / +0.001. So the gain is not confined to near-copies of anchors, but it is uneven and the verdict depends on where "far" starts. The pieces differ: the Laplacian regulariser's gain over aw8_all stays positive anchor-far (+0.013 / +0.027 AUC), the extra gain of the longer schedule is anchor-near (+0.021 / +0.018 there, +0.012 / −0.001 anchor-far with intervals that include zero), and the anchor-weight gain is as large anchor-far (AUC +0.020 / +0.034). A time-blocked split that removes a 25-frame buffer around held-out blocks of a run keeps the gain (development audit: AUC +0.026, accuracy +0.012). Development gains shrank on confirmation seeds by a median factor of 0.93 (range 0.50 to 2.42). A prospective test on new growth runs is the decisive next experiment.

## 4. Assumptions and limits

*Numbers carry markers and are verified by `check_prose.py`; tables are generated by `pp_limits.py`, `pp_strata.py`, `pp_wcurse.py` (see the Makefile).*

### 4.1 The same 168 groups, re-split
Every experiment of every branch draws from one labelled data set: 168 pair groups (521 judgments of which 51% are decisive, 14% ties and 35% "not applicable"), 284 distinct frames of 3 growth sessions (111, 108 and 65 frames). The comparison graph (frames as nodes, labelled groups as edges) falls into 117 connected components. A "new seed" changes the random split into initial / pool / validation / test groups, the random label draws and the training randomness; it never adds data. The held-out set of one seed has on average 63.5 (split A) or 53.2 (split B) decisive judgments. Consequences: (a) Wilcoxon p-values and bootstrap intervals over seeds describe the variability of splits, label draws and training, **not** sampling of new growth runs, so they are optimistic; (b) a pre-registered confirmation on unused seeds protects against selection on the development seeds, not against properties of these 168 groups; (c) per-type numbers, in particular HTR, rest on a handful of held-out judgments per seed and split.

### 4.2 Dense, near-duplicate frames
The frames are a nearly continuous sampling of three runs. Distances below are 1 − cosine similarity of the centred, normalised frozen SimCLR features (the geometry of the graph). The median distance of a held-out judgment's farther image to its nearest training image is 0.020 at budget 10 and 0.004 at budget 60; the nearer image is at 0.001 and 0.000 (median), and 97% of held-out judgments have an image within 0.01 of a training image at budget 60. For scale, the distance between two reference images of the same type has median 0.129, between different types 0.584. So test frames are not "new situations" but neighbours of training frames, which is exactly what a smoothness regulariser on a kNN graph can exploit. Strict de-duplication of the labelled data is not possible (red-team audit 2: at distance ≤ 0.002 only a minority of the candidate pool survives).

### 4.3 Anchor-near versus anchor-far judgments (secondary endpoint of every study)
The learners use typed ideal images ("anchors"); many of them are near-copies of trajectory frames. Of the 2359 held-out judgments of the red-team development block, 47% involve an image within 0.001 of some typed anchor (39% for the reference images alone), 22% have both images farther than 0.03 from every anchor ("anchor-far"; 29% for references alone). The **anchor-far secondary endpoint** is the AUC / accuracy computed on these judgments only. Reading, honestly (red-team **confirmation block**, 35 unused seeds; the development block, 20 seeds, is in the table as well): (i) the gain of the best learner over the tuned graph-free control is clearly positive in anchor-near judgments (+0.035 / +0.037 AUC), about zero in the bands between (0.001 to 0.01: +0.001 / −0.000; 0.01 to 0.03: −0.002 / −0.002) and positive again in anchor-far judgments (>0.03: +0.019 / +0.013 AUC with intervals above or touching zero, accuracy +0.029 / +0.029). With the red team's own threshold 0.01 the far stratum mixes the empty middle band into it and the AUC gain is +0.003 / +0.001: **the anchor-far verdict depends on the threshold**, and only about 12 judgments per (seed, budget, draw) cell lie beyond 0.03, so this stratum is noisy; the red team's frozen RT1 rule (threshold 0.01, one Holm family with its de-duplication and time-blocked tests) is its to report; (ii) by component: the Laplacian regulariser's gain over aw8_all stays positive anchor-far (>0.03: +0.013 / +0.027; >0.01: +0.009 / +0.010), whereas the extra gain of the four-fold schedule over lap3_k10 sits in anchor-near judgments (+0.021 / +0.018) and is not resolved anchor-far (+0.012 / −0.001 at >0.03; −0.003 / −0.006 at >0.01); (iii) the earlier anchor-weight gain (aw8_all over the default head) is as large in anchor-far judgments (+0.020 / +0.034) as anywhere, so it is not an anchor-copy artefact; (iv) a time-blocked evaluation (whole 100-frame blocks of a run held out, 25-frame buffer removed from training groups, candidate pool and graph; red-team audit 3, development block) keeps the gain: AUC +0.026 [+0.021, +0.031], accuracy +0.012 [+0.004, +0.020] over the tuned graph-free control, and +0.114 AUC over the shuffled-graph control (table `tables/redteam_extra.md`); this split still stays inside the three known runs. The strata of the red-team confirmation block are added to `tables/strata.csv` automatically once all of its per-judgment files exist (they did when this package was built).
**Only the red team's learners have an anchor-far version**: the confirmation cells of the individual studies store aggregated metrics only, so the claims of the other branches (GM, GE, selection) have no anchor-far check; re-running them with per-judgment output is listed in `GPU_TASKS_paper_package.md`.

### 4.4 Tuned on development seeds (winner's curse)
Every frozen candidate was chosen on development seeds that share the 168 groups with the confirmation seeds: the anchor weight 8, lambda 3 with k 10, the factor 4 and the graph-free control's schedule (steps ×2, learning rate ×0.5; chosen on 12 to 20 development seeds). The confirmation, not the development number, is the evidence; the typical shrinkage is small but single cells lose up to half of the development effect. The "tuned graph-free control" is tuned on one dimension only (steps and learning rate); other graph-free regularisers were tried only in development (consistency regularisation comes within −0.005 / −0.007 AUC of the best learner).

### 4.5 Other limits
- **Endpoint.** All learner and selection claims are about held-out preference judgments. On the paper's own endpoint (type accuracy of 28 ideal images) no learner or graph method beats 1-NN in a way attributable to the learner (claim G6); that endpoint cannot rank methods.
- **Controls are weak or narrow.** A shuffled graph is far worse than no graph (claim G3), so beating it is a low bar; the noisy-graph and non-graph controls are more informative but exist only for part of the claims.
- **Harsh splits.** The held-out-run and held-out-temperature tests use fixed test sets (50 and 26 judgments); the second confirmation block reuses the same test judgments, and test-group bootstrap intervals include zero in 7 of 8 cases.
- **Frozen features, CPU only.** Nothing was tested with an end-to-end fine-tuned encoder; the learner results are for a head on cached SimCLR features.
- **Selection** was examined single-shot from the initial model; sequential rounds with the best learner and selection from a cold start under `lap3_k10_st4` were not examined.
- **Branches not in the package yet.** Studies of other conversations that had no result files when this package was built (representation, anchor exchange, temporal graph) and the red team's confirmation block are not included; see the README for how to add them.


## 5. Integrity checks that are part of the build
- `pp_confirmations.py` recomputes every pre-registered test with each study's own test code and frozen spec; `tests/test_crosscheck.py` compares a sample with the numbers printed in the studies' own result documents.
- `pp_strata.py` asserts equality with the red team's `rt_tables.auc_by_stratum`.
- `pp_seedblocks.py` asserts that the 21 declared seed blocks are disjoint and that every confirmation directory contains only seeds of its declared block (`tables/seed_blocks.md`, `tables/inventory.md`).
- `pp_provenance.py` verifies pre-registration order from git history (`tables/prereg_order.md`); `check_prose.py` fails the build on any prose number that does not match a generated table.

## 6. Reproduce
`cd code/active_learning_studies/pair_disjoint_not_image_disjoint/graph_exploration/PAPER_PACKAGE && make all` (about 3 minutes on one core; needs numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib; no torch). See `README.md` there for the directory / seed block / branch map and `HANDOFF_paper_package.md` for what to do next.
